source_text:
ἀπολαύσωμεν πάντες, ἀγαπητοί, τῶν ἀγαθῶν χαρισμάτων ταύτης τῆς καλῆς πανηγύρεως· εἰσέλθωμεν χαίροντες εἰς
τὴν χαρὰν τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν ... ἄρχοντες καὶ ἀρχόμενοι ... πρεσβύτεροι μετὰ νεωτέρων, ἄνδρες καὶ γυναῖκες, πλούσιοι καὶ πένητες, δοῦλοι καὶ ἐλεύθεροι, δοξάσατε καὶ μεγαλύνατε κύριον τὸν θεὸν ἡμῶν καὶ τὴν λαμπρὰν ταύτην ἡμέραν καὶ φαιδρὰν ἐορτὴν ὑμνήσατε καὶ θαυμάσατε καὶ τιμήσατε, νηστεύοντες καὶ κοπιάσαντες ... ἐορτάσατε σήμερον. πλούσιοι καὶ πένητες μετὰ ἀλλήλων χορεύσατε, ἐγκρατεῖς καὶ ῥάθυμοι τὴν ἡμέραν τιμήσατε, νηστεύσαντες καὶ μὴ νηστεύσαντες εὐφράνθητε σήμερον· ἡ τράπεζα γέμει· μηδεὶς ἐξέλθῃ πεινῶν καὶ στερούμενος· πάντες ἀπολαύσατε τοῦ πλούτου τῆς χρηστότητος, ὅτι τὸ πάσχα ἡμῶν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐτύθη Χριστός· πάντες ἀντλήσατε ἐκ τῆς ἀκενώτου πηγῆς τοῦ σωτῆρος θεοῦ καὶ 1 εὐφράνθητε· γεύσασθε καὶ ἴδετε ὅτι Χριστὸς ὁ κύριος· θεὸς κύριος καὶ ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν· μηδεὶς θρηνείτω πενίαν· ἐφάνη γὰρ ἡ κοινὴ βασιλεία· μηδεὶς ὀδυρέσθω πταίσματα· συγγνώμη γὰρ ἀπὸ τοῦ τάφου ἀνέτειλε· μηδεὶς φοβείσθω τὸν θάνατον· 72 ἠλευθέρωσε γὰρ ἡμᾶς ὁ τοῦ σωτῆρος θάνατος. ἔσωσε γὰρ ἡμᾶς Χριστὸς ὁ θεὸς καὶ τοῦ ᾅδου ἐρρύσατο· ἐξήρπασεν ἡμᾶς ἐκ τῆς καταδυναστείας τοῦ διαβόλου καὶ τῆς δουλείας αὐτοῦ ἠλευθέρωσεν· ἐπικράνθη ὁ ᾅδης γευσάμενος τῆς τιμίας καὶ ἁγίας σαρκὸς τοῦ δεσπότου καθὼς Ἡσαΐας προεῖπεν· ἐπικράνθη ὁ Ἅιδης συναντήσας σοι κάτω· ἐπικράνθη· καὶ γὰρ κατηργήθη· ἐπικράνθη· καὶ γὰρ ἐνεπαίχθη· ἐπικράνθη· καὶ γὰρ ἐδεσμεύθη· ἔλαβε σῶμα καὶ θεῷ περιέτυχεν· ἔλαβεν ὅπερ ἔβλεπε καὶ πέπτωκεν ὅθεν οὐκ ἔβλεπε· κατέπιεν ὁ θάνατος ἀγνοῶν, καὶ καταπιὼν ἔγνω ὃν κατέπιεν· κατέπιεν ζωήν, κατεπόθη ὑπὸ τῆς ζωῆς· κατέπιεν τὸν ἕνα μετὰ πάντων, ἀπώλεσε τὸν ἕνα διὰ τοὺς πάντας. ἥρπασεν ὡς λέων, συνεθλάσθη δὲ τοὺς ὀδόντας. διὰ τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὁ θάνατος ἴσχυεν· ἐν Χριστῷ δὲ ἁμαρτίαν μὴ εὑρὼν ἀνενέργητος ἔμεινεν. εὔκαιρον οὖν εἰπεῖν· ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ κέντρον, ποῦ σου, ᾅδη, τὸ νῖκος; ἀνέστη Χριστὸς καὶ σὺ καταβέβλησαι· ἀνέστη Χριστὸς καὶ χαίρουσιν ἄγγελοι· ἀνέστη Χριστὸς καὶ πεπτώκασι δαίμονες. 73 ἀνέστη Χριστὸς καὶ φθορᾶς ἐλυτρώθημεν· ἀνέστη Χριστὸς καὶ κατάρας ἐρρύσθημεν· ἀνέστη Χριστὸς καὶ ἡμεῖς συνανέστημεν· ἀνέστη Χριστὸς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐζωώθημεν· Χριστὸς ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστὰς ἀπαρχὴ τῶν κεκοιμημένων ἐγένετο· αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος καὶ ἡ προσκύνησις καὶ ἡ μεγαλοσύνη νῦν καὶ ἀεὶ καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. ἀμήν.
thought_title: Invitation to the feast and Christ's victory over death
orientation: The preacher, having praised God for trampling death and granting eternal life, now turns directly to the congregation, inviting everyone to share in the Easter feast and proclaiming Christ's victory over Hades and death.
pass_a_gloss: Let us all enjoy, beloved, the good gifts of this beautiful festival; let us enter rejoicing into the joy of our Lord ... rulers and ruled ... elders with younger ones, men and women, rich and poor, slaves and free, glorify and magnify the Lord our God and hymn and marvel at and honor this bright day and radiant feast, you who fasted and labored ... celebrate today. Rich and poor, dance with one another; self-controlled and careless, honor the day; you who fasted and did not fast, be glad today; the table is full; let no one go out hungry and deprived; all of you enjoy the wealth of goodness, because our Passover, Christ, was sacrificed for us; all of you draw from the inexhaustible spring of the Savior God and be glad; taste and see that Christ is the Lord; the Lord is God and has appeared to us; let no one lament poverty; for the common kingdom has appeared; let no one grieve over sins; for forgiveness has dawned from the tomb; let no one fear death; for the death of the Savior has set us free. For Christ God saved us and rescued us from Hades; he snatched us from the tyranny of the devil and freed us from his slavery; Hades was embittered when he tasted the precious and holy flesh of the Master, as Isaiah foretold; Hades was embittered when he met you below; he was embittered; for he was also abolished; he was embittered; for he was also mocked; he was embittered; for he was also bound; he took a body and encountered God; he took what he saw and fell by what he did not see; death swallowed in ignorance, and having swallowed he knew whom he swallowed; he swallowed life, he was swallowed by life; he swallowed the one with all, he lost the one for the sake of all. He seized like a lion, but his teeth were crushed. Through sin death had strength; but in Christ, finding no sin, it remained ineffective. It is timely therefore to say: Where, death, is your sting, where, Hades, is your victory? Christ is risen and you have been cast down; Christ is risen and angels rejoice; Christ is risen and demons have fallen. Christ is risen and we have been redeemed from corruption; Christ is risen and we have been rescued from the curse; Christ is risen and we have risen with him; Christ is risen and we have been made alive; Christ, risen from the dead, has become the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep; to him be the glory and the power and the worship and the majesty now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.why: Glossary requires 'table' for τράπεζα; γέμει means 'is full/laden', conveying the abundance of the feast.

choices.term: τὸ πάσχα ἡμῶν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐτύθη Χριστός
choices.english: our Passover, Christ, was sacrificed for us
choices.why: Glossary requires 'Passover' for πάσχα; the word order emphasizes 'our Passover' as the subject, with Christ in apposition, matching 1 Corinthians 5:7.
rejected: Christ our Paschal feast was sacrificed for us
our Pascha was sacrificed, Christ, for us

choices.term: ἐκ τῆς ἀκενώτου πηγῆς τοῦ σωτῆρος θεοῦ
choices.english: from the inexhaustible spring of the Savior God
choices.why: Glossary requires 'spring' for πηγή; ἀκενώτου means 'inexhaustible', emphasizing the endless supply of divine grace.
rejected: from the unfailing fountain of the Savior God
from the inexhaustible source of the Savior God

choices.term: συγγνώμη γὰρ ἀπὸ τοῦ τάφου ἀνέτειλε
choices.english: for forgiveness has dawned from the tomb
choices.why: συγγνώμη means 'forgiveness/pardon'; ἀνέτειλε means 'has risen/dawned', using the imagery of light emerging from the tomb.
rejected: for pardon has sprung from the tomb
for absolution has arisen from the tomb

choices.why: Glossary requires 'Hades' for ᾅδης; ἐπικράνθη is the aorist passive of πικραίνω, 'was embittered', echoing Isaiah's prophecy of Hades' bitter reaction.

choices.english: firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep
choices.why: Glossary requires 'firstfruits' for ἀπαρχή; κεκοιμημένων is the perfect participle of κοιμάω, 'those who have fallen asleep', the standard Pauline phrase for the dead in Christ.
rejected: first portion of those who have fallen asleep
first offering of the sleeping ones

bible_refs.note: τὸ πάσχα ἡμῶν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐτύθη Χριστός
γεύσασθε καὶ ἴδετε ὅτι Χριστὸς ὁ κύριος (adapted from 'taste and see that the Lord is good')
ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ κέντρον, ποῦ σου, ᾅδη, τὸ νῖκος
Χριστὸς ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστὰς ἀπαρχὴ τῶν κεκοιμημένων ἐγένετο

pass_b_english: Let us all enjoy, beloved, the good gifts of this beautiful festival. Let us enter with rejoicing into the joy of our Lord—rulers and ruled, elders with the young, men and women, rich and poor, slaves and free. Glorify and magnify the Lord our God, and sing hymns to this bright and radiant day, and marvel at it and honor it, whether you have fasted or labored—celebrate today. Rich and poor, dance together. You who are disciplined and you who are careless, honor the day. You who have fasted and you who have not, rejoice today. The table is full; let no one leave hungry or deprived. Let everyone enjoy the wealth of God's goodness, for our Passover, Christ, was sacrificed for us (1 Corinthians 5:7). Let everyone draw from the inexhaustible spring of the Savior God and rejoice. Taste and see that Christ is the Lord (Psalm 33:9 LXX, Psalm 34:8 Hebrew). The Lord is God, and he has appeared to us (Psalm 117:27 LXX, Psalm 118:27 Hebrew). Let no one mourn over poverty, for the common kingdom has appeared. Let no one grieve over sins, for forgiveness has dawned from the tomb. Let no one fear death, for the Savior's death has set us free.

Christ our God has saved us and rescued us from Hades. He snatched us from the tyranny of the devil and freed us from his slavery. Hades was embittered when it tasted the precious and holy flesh of the Master, as Isaiah foretold: "Hades was embittered when it met you below. It was embittered, for it was abolished. It was embittered, for it was mocked. It was embittered, for it was bound. It received a body and encountered God. It received what it saw and fell by what it did not see." Death swallowed without knowing, and in swallowing it came to know whom it had swallowed. It swallowed life, and it was swallowed up by life. It swallowed the one along with all, and it lost the one for the sake of all. It seized like a lion, but its teeth were crushed. Through sin death had power, but finding no sin in Christ, it remained ineffective. So it is fitting to say: "O death, where is your sting? O Hades, where is your victory?" (1 Corinthians 15:55). Christ is risen, and you are cast down. Christ is risen, and the angels rejoice. Christ is risen, and the demons have fallen. Christ is risen, and we have been delivered from corruption. Christ is risen, and we have been rescued from the curse. Christ is risen, and we have risen with him. Christ is risen, and we have been made alive. Christ, risen from the dead, has become the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep (1 Corinthians 15:20). To him be glory and power and worship and majesty, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
notes: The source contains ellipses marked by '...' after 'τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν' and after 'κοπιάσαντες', indicating omitted text in the manuscript or edition.

last_rejected.source_quote: γεύσασθε καὶ ἴδετε ὅτι Χριστὸς ὁ κύριος
last_rejected.why: The citation should be Psalm 33:9 LXX (Psalm 34:8 Hebrew) for 'Taste and see that the Lord is good', but the text quotes 'Christ is the Lord', a modified form.
last_rejected.fix: Psalm 33:9 LXX (Psalm 34:8 Hebrew), adapted by the homilist.
last_rejected.ruling: Citation correctly identifies the LXX Psalm being adapted; 'Christ is the Lord' is the preacher's modification, not a wrong reference.

last_rejected.why: The citation should be Psalm 117:26-27 LXX (Psalm 118:26-27 Hebrew) for 'God is the Lord and has appeared to us'.
last_rejected.ruling: Psalm 117:27 LXX correctly cited for 'θεὸς κύριος καὶ ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν'; including v.26 is unnecessary, not an error.

last_rejected.quote: whether you have fasted or labored
last_rejected.why: κοπιάσαντες means 'toiled/worked hard', not 'labored' in sense of physical labor; context is ascetic effort. 'Labored' is ambiguous.
last_rejected.fix: whether you have fasted or toiled.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Labored' is within normal range of κοπιάσαντες; 'toiled' is a preference, not a major error.

last_rejected.why: ἀνενέργητος means 'powerless, inactive, without effect'—death lost its power, not merely became 'ineffective'.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Ineffective' is within normal range of ἀνενέργητος; 'powerless' is a preference, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: Christ is risen, and we have been delivered from corruption
last_rejected.why: ἐλυτρώθημεν means 'we were ransomed', not 'delivered'. Glossary fixes 'ransom' for λύτρον.
last_rejected.fix: we have been ransomed from corruption.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Delivered' is within normal range of ἐλυτρώθημεν; glossary preference for 'ransom' does not make it a major error.
